Completeness and contamination of each bin, estimated with CheckM, and selection of the most complete bins for further analysis. Commands for this step were run in `checkm/`.

## **Step 4: Check bin quality with checkm**

Moved into the `checkm` folder

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm
```

Listed the lengths of all contigs in the assembly, sorted from shortest to longest, to find the longest contig. its name is `contig_126`

```{bash}
cat ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n
```

Copied all the bins, including the longest contig, into `checkm/bins_bbd`.

```{bash}
samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_126 > ../metabat/bins_bbd/contig_126.fa
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/
```

Made a slurm script, [run_checkm_bbd.sh](checkm/run_checkm_bbd.sh) and saved it in `checkm`.

CheckM was run with the `lineage_wf` workflow on the `.fa` files in `bins_bbd`, using 6 threads, and results were written to `checkm_results_bbd.txt`

Submitted the job (job 492). It ran for abut an hour.

```{bash}
sbatch run_checkm_bbd.sh
```

## **Step 5: Select bins based on checkm results**

The aim of the functional analysis is to answer two questions: who is there (which taxonomic groups are present), and what can they do (which genes and pathways they have).

Moved back into `checkm` and viewed the results with `head`

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm
```

```{bash}
head checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```

try viewing more of the results:

```{bash}
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```

Chose to focus on bins with completeness above 15%

Used `awk` to print the lines where column 13 (completeness) is above 15, then only the bin ID (column 1)

```{bash}
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15'
```

```{bash}
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}'
```

Saved the bin ID's to `bbd_topbins.txt` for the next step.

```{bash}
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt
```
